newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian FSB Bank raises capital base.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian FSB Bank raises capital base.

text.p: Nigerian commercial bank FSB International Bank on Thursday announced a scrip issue of eight new shares for three in a bid to raise its capital base to one billion naira from 300 million naira.

Stock dealers said FSB would be the first quoted bank to hit the one billion naira capital base, exceeding the 500 million naira prescribed by the authorities for Nigerian banks in a radical change announced in the fiscal 1997 budget in January.
Banks have until the end of 1998 to comply with the nine-fold increase in their capital base geared to strengthen them.
FSB said its authorised share capital will rise to one billion naira made up of two billion ordinary shares.
An extraordinary general meeting where shareholders are expected to approve the proposal is scheduled to be held in Lagos on March 26.
"FSB wants to stay ahead of the competition," said dealer Tunde Ayeni of CSL Stockbrokers.
The highest capitalised bank on the stock market now is Union Bank with a capital base of 793 million naira.
Brokers said unquoted Nigerian International Bank -- now fully-owned by U.S.-based Citibank, had an authorised share capital of 750 million naira.
FSB shares were adjusted for the new shares on Thursday, closing at 2.39 naira, down from its previous 8.75 naira.
Together with other banking shares, FSB stocks have made generous gains since January when government asked the banks to shore up their capital bases.
Most investors have been rushing to buy to benefit from anticipated bonus and rights issues, according to analysts.
Traders and analysts said the nation's bigger banks were poised to implement the new limit soon and would also achieve the billion naira capital base easily.
